For a constrained route problem, only a small fraction of those strings may encode feasible routes. Low feasible-sampling probability is therefore plausible, but it has several possible causes: dilution induced by the representation, an uncontrolled penalty scale, classical optimizer failure, misalignment between the training loss and feasible entry, or a genuine limitation of the variational family. These mechanisms lead to different scientific conclusions and should be separated before shallow-QAOA failure is interpreted.

The strongest positive evidence comes from the preregistered held-out study: 84 tasks on 15 nonoverlapping base graphs. At the preregistered graph analysis unit, the O3-minus-O0 effect in logarithmic feasibility gain is +0.3547 decades, with one-sided 95\% lower bound +0.2374 and Holm-adjusted exact sign-flip p=2.4410^-4. Against the O2 capacity control, the effect is -0.0086 decades with lower bound -0.0360, above the preregistered non-inferiority margin of -0.10 decades. As secondary outcomes, O3 increases optimal-route probability on 80 of 84 tasks and increases both feasible and optimal-route probability on 79 of 84.

Let G=(V,E) be a directed graph with source s, target t, positive objective cost c_e, and nonnegative resource consumption r_e for every edge e E. For a directed s--t path P, the single-resource RCSP used in this study is equation _P\; C(P)=_e Pc_e subject to R(P)=_e Pr_e B, eq:rcsp equation where B is the resource budget. RCSP is a standard constrained-routing problem beasley1989rcsp; our controlled instances are synthetic layered directed acyclic graphs rather than road-network deployments.

The task generator creates a singleton source layer, one or more internal layers, and a singleton target layer. Edges point forward by one or two layers, with a deterministic coverage set ensuring that every node participates in a source--target route. Additional edges are sampled without replacement until the prescribed edge count is reached. Edge costs are positive integers in [1,9] and edge resources are positive integers in [1,1000]. Generation is deterministic under a master seed. The v2 universe uses five base graphs at each target edge count m\7,10,13,16,19\.

The scaling study was designed before its QAOA outcomes were generated. It contains five base graphs at each edge-bit size m\12,14,16,18,20,22\ and six distinct feasible-route cardinalities per graph, for 180 tasks in total. Base indices 0--3 at m=12--18 form the development set; index 4 at those sizes forms an interpolation holdout; all five graphs at m=20,22 form the extrapolation holdout. Task generation, model candidates, model selection, resource guards, and objective comparisons were specified without using predecessor QAOA outcomes.

The prospective resource guard benchmarked fixed-parameter statevector kernels before optimization. At m=22, it predicted 520 MiB per worker and 2249.3 seconds for one full optimization, above the specified 1200-second guard. The entire m=22 size was therefore marked resource-censored before QAOA optimization. The 180 planned depth-two/depth-three cells remain visible in the denominator; they are neither scientific failures nor imputed outcomes.
